notes.body: Arashi is simply storm — rain and wind outside the door. The same bare word returns later in the evening.

variants.body: Japanese arashi: a storm of rain and wind, stated here as bare perception with no verb beyond sounding. The house keeps the same plain word for its two later returns, when the family is too noisy to hear it and when it is heard again quietly and whispered at the close; it is the outside evening passing, not a symbol to underline.

notes.body: Table renders 卓 marked with ruby テーブル to mean a low dining table, and dark electric light is a single dim early domestic bulb hung against the wall.
notes.span: at the {t:table} under {t:electric-light} hanging against the wall of the narrow room

variants.body: Source writes 卓 with ruby テーブル (teeburu), fixing the reading as table rather than desk: the low table around which the family gathers, clears things under, drums, feeds, and later clears up. Dark electric light (kurai dentō) is period lighting — one dim bulb in a narrow room — kept dim/dark rather than modern bright light. Historical kana てろた in surrounding narration marks ongoing states and acts.

notes.body: A drowsy peace renders まどろむやうな安らかさ, the first sounding of the book's recurring peace/rest chord that later hardens into doctrine.
sources: p3 まどろむやうな安らかさ

data.say: No casual notes needed; curious keeps two frame-and-room glosses, student adds ruby and rest-chord detail.
